title: Creative Strategy
summary: AVIA's pipeline is too thin to scale, with one brief ready for launch in the last seven days against five the week before. MAIA ran at 0.79 seven-day ROAS against a 0.85 to 0.90 target and a $110 to $120 cost per new customer. Production is about 150 concepts a week, toward roughly 1,000 a month across both brands, with a shift to unaware ads.
points: Strategist ROAS over seven days: Elissa 0.81, Adarsha 0.79, Lucas 0.78 on about $100,000 spend
MAIA had 25 to 26 briefs ready for launch and 130 new briefs, up from 92
Editor capacity: two more editors for Lucas, Denver moves to Peter, Elissa stays at about 15 a week
Black Friday: banners, statics and bottom-of-funnel creative first; offer changes would be front-end gifts
A competitor's cease and desist removed the Cosmos study from use
Unaware ads hit 25% with $88,000 spend from four wins, against 53 wins for $123,000 in aware ads
decisions: Put the emphasis on AVIA output and raise the AVIA budget
No specific flavanol amounts (milligrams) and no Mars-funded studies; 'high flavanols' is fine
Tone down artery-plaque claims (about 10% of spend) after FDA lawyer advice
Formats to push: AI animation, AI UGC, AI authority, VSL and AI drama, mostly unaware
Switch to a stronger editor when an editor cannot deliver a format
